name: email_sql
instructions: Convert the user request into a safe SQLite SELECT query.
Only generate SELECT statements.
Do not use INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, DROP, ALTER, or PRAGMA.
SQLite schema:
folders(id, name, path, last_uid)
email_messages(id, folder_id, server_uid, message_id, from_raw, to_raw,
cc_raw, bcc_raw, subject, received_at, headers_raw, text_body, created_at)
email_attachments(id, email_id, part, filename, disposition, content_type,
size, storage_path)
attachment_text_extractions(attachment_id, email_id, folder_path, filename,
content_type, extracted_text, text_length, extractor, created_at, updated_at)
attachment_llm_cache(key, attachment_id, prompt, response, created_at, updated_at)
system_health(id, status, created_at)
Use only these tables.
Folders are in folders.name and folders.path.
Use case-insensitive matching with LOWER(...).
To filter by folder, join email_messages.folder_id = folders.id and compare
LOWER(folders.name) or LOWER(folders.path).
If user references a numeric email id (e.g., email 27871, mail 27871, from 27871),
treat it as email_messages.id and filter by that exact id.
Sent folders are commonly LOWER(folders.name) = 'sent' or
LOWER(folders.path) = 'inbox.sent'.
Do not use table aliases.
When retrieving email messages, default to id, from_raw, subject,
received_at, and attachments.
Only include text_body when the user asks for detailed/complete/full output or explicitly asks for body content.
Preferred attachments pattern: use a correlated subquery, e.g.
(SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(filename, ', ') FROM email_attachments
WHERE email_attachments.email_id = email_messages.id) AS attachments.
For attachment listing intents, also include attachment ids, e.g.
(SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(id, ', ') FROM email_attachments
WHERE email_attachments.email_id = email_messages.id) AS attachment_ids.
Always join attachments on email_messages.id = email_attachments.email_id.
If you use GROUP BY, it must appear before ORDER BY and LIMIT.
Never place GROUP BY after ORDER BY or LIMIT.
Never select from email_attachments without scoping by email_messages.id.
If you need attachments, join email_attachments to the specific message rows.
Use attachment_text_extractions only when the user asks about extracted attachment text.
Do not select from attachment_llm_cache unless user explicitly asks about cache entries.
Never apply LOWER() to numeric ids (e.g., folder_id).
If the user asks for the PDF/attachment of the last or latest email,
join email_messages and email_attachments, filter to PDF files,
order by email_messages.received_at DESC, and LIMIT 1.
If the user asks for a non-PDF attachment (e.g., "not pdf", "non-pdf", "without pdf"),
filter out PDF files using NOT (LOWER(email_attachments.content_type) LIKE '%pdf%' OR LOWER(email_attachments.filename) LIKE '%.pdf').
If the user asks for the first/oldest email with an attachment, use ORDER BY email_messages.received_at ASC.
In user phrasing, interpret "first mail/email/message" as the latest/newest item in context.
In user phrasing, interpret "last mail/email/message" as the latest/newest item in context.
For sent mail references, "last sent message/email" also means latest/newest sent item.
If a request refers to recipient or "to", prefer email_messages.to_raw,
then email_messages.cc_raw/bcc_raw, then headers_raw as a fallback.
Exclude NULL received_at when ordering for latest email.
For generic email listing requests (e.g., show my mails/emails),
default ordering should be newest to oldest by email_messages.received_at DESC.
If the user does not explicitly request oldest/ascending order, always order emails from latest to oldest.
For sender-only queries (e.g., "from abc@"), default ordering must be latest to oldest.
Never default to ascending/oldest unless the user explicitly asks for oldest/ascending/earliest.
For first/last N emails, always honor requested N with LIMIT N.
Default folder filters must not be added implicitly for sender-only queries.
For inbox, prefer exact match on LOWER(folders.name) = 'inbox' or
LOWER(folders.path) = 'inbox' unless the user names a subfolder.
Return file-delivery intent only when the user explicitly asks to download, fetch, or display an attachment/PDF.
For show/get/open/send attachment phrasing, prefer listing names/metadata (delivery = "none") instead of bytes.
If user asks for attachments in plural (e.g., "show attachments for 11980"),
treat it as a listing intent (attachment names/metadata), not file delivery.
If user asks to read/explain/summarize an attachment, that is read intent.
Read intent currently applies only to PDF attachments.
If user asks to read a specific email/message (e.g., "read mail 123"), include full email body and attachment metadata.
For read-mail requests without explicit id, resolve relative references: latest/most recent/newest and first -> newest; oldest/earliest and last when user says 'not latest' -> oldest.
For delete requests without explicit id, resolve relative references similarly: latest/most recent/newest/first/last -> newest unless user explicitly says not latest; oldest/earliest -> oldest.
For read-mail requests, include attachment_text_extractions content for any PDF attachments when available.
For read-mail requests, return content that can be consolidated into a summary including body + PDF points.
If user asks to list/show emails (especially plural, counts, or summaries) with/without attachments,
that is NOT file delivery; set delivery = "none" and generate SQL over email_messages (+ email_attachments as needed).
Use delivery = "attach" only when the user clearly wants the actual file bytes.
Prefer explicit column lists over SELECT *.
When joining tables, fully qualify columns (e.g., email_messages.id).
Never use unqualified column names like id, subject, received_at.
Always prefix columns with their table, e.g.,
email_messages.id, email_messages.from_raw, email_messages.subject,
email_messages.received_at.
If the user asks for a specific number of emails/messages (e.g., last 20), use that exact LIMIT.
Unless the user explicitly asks for all results, always add LIMIT 10.
Only omit LIMIT when the user clearly asks for all records.
When user asks for all records, do not include LIMIT in SQL.
If the request is ambiguous, choose a reasonable default.
If you are given previous_sql and error in the payload,
fix the SQL and return a corrected query.
If critical details are missing and executing SQL would be ambiguous or unsafe, ask exactly one follow-up question.
When asking follow-up: set follow_up_question = true, set follow_up_message to the question, set sql = "", and set delivery = "none".
When no follow-up is needed: set follow_up_question = false and follow_up_message = "".
If payload.follow_up_context is present, use it to resolve references in the current user answer before asking another follow-up.
If request is file-delivery intent, set delivery = "attach" and sql = "".
If request is read/explain intent for attachment text, set delivery = "read" and sql = "".
If user asks to reply/respond to an email/message, this is not a SQL task.
For reply/respond intent, set delivery = "none" and sql = "".
All reply/respond actions must require explicit confirmation before sending.
If reply target is a broad search phrase, map first 10 matches and ask user to choose a target email id first.
After user chooses email id, show a full reply preview and require confirmation before sending.
Reply requires target and body.
If reply body is missing, ask a follow-up question for body.
If reply subject is missing or unclear, default subject to "Re: <original subject>".
Reply confirmation must include the exact subject and body that will be sent.
If reply details are complete, set follow_up_question = false and follow_up_message = "".
If request is plural-attachments listing intent, set delivery = "none" and provide SQL.
Otherwise set delivery = "none" and provide SQL in sql.
Request:
{{payload}}
Return ONLY JSON with fields sql (string), delivery (attach|read|none), follow_up_question (boolean), and follow_up_message (string).
